I'm recreating this badge scene live in an iOS app (RealityKit). The app builds
its own lighting and floor; it only imports the badge USDZ. Using
/Users/antonioperedo/Desktop/badges/medallion/silver_medallion_stage_refined.blend,
please produce the following and tell me every file path you write. Do not
modify the original .blend; work on a copy.

1. Baked environment map (most important). RealityKit cannot use rectangular
   area lights; metal reflections come from an image-based light instead.
   Render a 360 degree equirectangular EXR (Cycles, panoramic camera) from the
   badge's center (0, 0, 0) with the badge, floor and haze hidden, so the five
   rectangle lights and the spotlight appear as the bright shapes they are in
   reflections. Make the light rectangles visible to camera rays (emission)
   for this bake only. 2048x1024, linear, no view transform. Also export a
   second version at 1024x512.

2. The grow-and-spin animation, as data. For every animated object (badge,
   camera, lights), list: which properties are keyframed (location, rotation,
   scale), the rotation axis and order, every keyframe (frame number and
   value), the interpolation and easing of each F-curve (bezier handles or
   easing type), frame range and fps. Say whether the badge rotates or the
   camera orbits, and whether any light is parented to the badge or camera.

3. A lighter badge export for mobile. Save a copy of the badge as a new USDZ:
   decimate to about 40,000 triangles total while keeping the rim, bevels and
   emblem facets crisp (decimate flat and interior areas most; keep hard edges
   with custom normals or edge split); keep the six meshes and their names;
   resize textures to 512x512 except the emblem and inset normal maps
   (keep 1024); report the triangle count per mesh and the final file size.
   Confirm normal maps are OpenGL convention (green up).

4. Materials detail. For each of the 8 materials, list the full Principled BSDF
   values actually used in the render, including anisotropy, anisotropic
   rotation and the tangent/direction source for the brushed steel (is the
   brushing circumferential via anisotropy, a texture, or both), coat, sheen,
   and any node setup that did NOT survive the USDZ export (procedural
   textures, bump nodes, color ramps, layer weights, fresnel mixes). For
   anything lost, describe what it did visually.

5. Reference renders. Render these exact frames from the current scene (beam
   hidden as it is now) as 16-bit PNG 1080x1440: the final face-on frame, a
   frame at about 45 degrees of spin, a nearly edge-on frame, and the frame
   where the badge is about half size. Also render the final face-on frame
   twice more: once with View Transform "Standard" instead of AgX, and once
   with the Glare node muted. Give the frame number of each.

6. Contact shadow and glow. Is there any shadow or occlusion under the badge
   on the floor (beyond the reflection)? If so, bake it to a 512x512 PNG
   texture on the floor plane, cropped to the area near the badge, with
   transparency. Also confirm the Glare node settings are the only
   post-processing.

7. Per-tier differences. If other tiers (iron, copper, bronze, steel, gold,
   platinum, diamond) will reuse this model, which materials change per tier
   and which stay shared?

Follow-up for the RealityKit badge recreation. The app lights the badge with
your 360 EXR, but flat emblem facets come out as flat tones (pure white or
black) because an environment map is infinitely distant. I'm adding real
point/spot lights at your light positions and applying your AgX look in the
app. To match it, please produce the following from a copy of
silver_medallion_stage_refined.blend (do not modify the original) and list
every file path you write.

1. Per-light solo renders. Frame 360, beam hidden as now, 1080x1440, each of
   the six lights rendered ALONE (all other lights and the world off), plus
one
   render with ONLY the world environment on. Save each as linear
scene-referred
   EXR (no view transform, no glare), same exposure for all, so they add up to
   the full image. Name files by light.

2. Full-size pose references. With the badge's scale locked to 1 and its
   position at Y = 0 (growth disabled), render these rotations about +Y: 0,
20,
   45, 70, 90, 135, 180 degrees, 1080x1440. For each, save both an AgX Medium
   High Contrast PNG exactly like the final render (with glare) and a linear
   EXR with no view transform and no glare.

3. AgX look as a LUT. Export the exact view transform used (AgX, Medium High
   Contrast, exposure 0, gamma 1) as a 3D LUT in .cube format, 33 or 65 points,
   mapping scene-linear Rec.709 input to display sRGB output. State the input
   range and any shaper or log encoding it expects (AgX needs a log shaper for
   HDR input; include the shaper as a separate 1D .cube or give its exact
   formula and range). Verify it: apply the LUT to your linear frame-360 EXR
   and report the max per-channel difference against the real AgX render.

4. Per-light detail the app needs. For each of the six lights: Blender's
   per-light Diffuse, Specular (Glossy), Transmission and Volume factors;
   area-light Spread; spotlight blend and size; whether shadows are cast
   (and soft-shadow radius); and any light-linking or light-group setup.

5. Emblem shading check. Are the emblem facets flat-shaded (one normal per
   face) or smooth / auto-smooth? Does the emblem normal map do anything
   visible at 400 px on screen? Show a frame-360 render with the emblem normal
   map disconnected, cropped to the emblem.

6. Glare exactly. Confirm the Fog Glow's effective radius in pixels at
   1080x1440 for size 0.6, and whether it runs before or after the view
   transform (on scene-linear or display values).
